en: Regarding the ritual for making offerings to the Eight World-Protecting Devas,
the *Susiddhikara Sūtra*, compiled by the Śramaṇa Fazun of Qinglong Monastery,
states: "Those who cultivate the practices of mantra and conduct should daily make offerings to the deities who protect the directions."
If one invokes the deities, there will be no calamities.
[One should perform this] in the eight directions outside the *maṇḍala*.
Spread either *kuśa* grass or lotus leaves,
or smear a circular altar to form ten positions;
place the gods Brahmā and Earth on the left and right of Śakra.
If there is no place to establish the boundary outside the maṇḍala,
one should instead establish a square boundary in a clean and secluded area in front of the maṇḍala; within that space,
one should remain facing the eight directions.
Place the deities Brahmā and Mahendra in the center,
and offer food to the deities of the ten directions;
for this purpose, one should use various kinds of gruel.
That is to say, non-glutinous rice and sesame seeds.
First, place a clean leaf so that it is utterly pure,
and set fragrant, delicious offerings in a vessel.
Before sitting, first place a clean leaf or a clean tea bowl.
First, fill a pure flask with scented water;
then, kneel with the right knee on the ground and join the palms.
I invoke the worldly deities of the ten directions.
I respectfully invite the Lord Kauśika of the East, together with his retinue, to descend here.
May you graciously accept the offerings I have prepared.
I respectfully invite the Fire Mountain King of the southeastern direction and his retinue to descend here;
may you graciously accept the offerings I have prepared.
I respectfully invite the Lord Yama of the southern direction.
The Lord of Rākṣasas,
the Heavenly King of the Bhūtas,
and the Nāga King Varuṇa.
The Wind Deity King and others,
the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa,
and the Heavenly King Īśāna.
Great Brahmā Deva King,
I respectfully invite all the great deva kings who dwell upon the earth, together with their retinues, to descend here.
I pray that you will graciously accept the offerings I have prepared.
I humbly pray that you will secretly bestow your protection upon me.
Having addressed my request to the deities of the original direction as visualized, I now withdraw and take my leave.
Next, invoke the World-Protecting Deity (Lokapāla) by his Brahma-name.

For Īśāna in the northeast, together with his retinue of bhūtas, the mudrā is the trident seal: form the *samaya-muṣṭi* and extend the fire-finger (*teja-aṅguli*), bending it back against the back of the wind-finger (*vāyu-aṅguli*).
The mantra of Īśāna is as follows:
*Namo samantabuddhānāṃ rudrāya svāhā.* Visualize that the Heavenly Kings who protect the directions each descend from their celestial palaces and arrive here.
Based on the original directions, mark the mind and cause it to abide.
This is the Seal of Śakra:
form the inner fist (*antarbandha*), extend the two wind-fingers (*vāyu-aṅguli*) like needles.
The mantra of Śakra, King of Devas, is: *Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ śakrāya svāhā*. Agni-rishi.
In the mudrā of concentration, the thumbs and ring fingers are joined to form a triangle;
the wisdom hand has its four fingers extended upward with the middle finger crossing horizontally across the palm;
the wind [finger] is bent at the third joint.
The mantra of the Fire Deity is:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānām āgneye svāhā*. [Visualize] the union of concentration and wisdom upon the earth, wind, and back, entering the moon.
The mantra of King Yama is:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ vavavasadaye svāhā*. The rākṣasa has a terrifying form.
In the southwest, he holds a sword.
The mantra is: *Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ raudraśāntiprada svāhā*. Varuṇa holds a noose.
The mantra is: *Namaḥ samantabuddhānām āpātaye svāhā*. For Vāyu (the Wind Deity), form the *vajra-kuñci* (wisdom-fist) mudrā; for Earth and Water, extend the fingers upward.
The mantra of Vāyu is:
Namo samantabuddhānāṃ vāyave svāhā. Forming the *tathāgata-muṣṭi* with palms joined, place the two ring fingers (*anāmikā*) inside the palms with their tips crossed.
The empty [space] is vertical, the wind [element] is tilted and bent one inch away so that they do not touch.
The mantra of the Heavenly King Vaisravana is: *Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ vaiśramaṇāya svāhā*. Brahmā holds a red lotus; the space [element] holds water in samādhi.
The mantra of Brahmā is:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ prajñāpāramitāyai svāhā*. The Earth Deity holds a precious vase.

The mantra of the Earth Deity is: *Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ prativedyai svāhā*. The Sun Deity holds the wheel of fire with his hands joined in the mudrā of merit and wisdom, facing upward; the Water Deity enters into space; the Earth Deity holds the wheel of earth; and the Fire Deity has his hands joined in the mudrā of desire. The Water and Fire deities hold each other’s hands.
The mantra is: Namaḥ samantabuddhānām, anityāya svāhā. The Moon Deity holds a white lotus flower in his hand.
Form the *śūnyatā-muṣṭi* mudrā with the first finger. The mantra is:
*Namo samantabuddhānāṃ jñānaye svāhā*. [Insert name here] respectfully addresses you.
The World-Protecting Heavenly Kings, the deities of the twelve zodiacal mansions,
the nine planetary lords, the twenty-eight lunar lodgings,
and the natal stars of one’s karmic destiny.
Now that I have encountered this calamity,
I respectfully offer thanks to the assembly of devas for their assistance in such-and-such matters,
and I shall comply with the Buddha’s instructions.
Having accepted my invitation,
they all came to attend this assembly; responding to this call,
they single-mindedly gave rise to a heart of joy.
"May you pacify and eliminate calamities and obstacles for me, [Name],
and increase my merit, blessings,
and lifespan. Or say:
From this day forward, I shall practice the mantra.
Relying upon the power of the Great Sage’s protective mindfulness,
may I deliver all sentient beings from the karmic suffering of saṃsāra.
I pray that the World-Protecting Lord of Devas, who traverses the sky with the lunar mansions and planets,
will follow the Buddha’s teachings, bestow fearlessness upon me, and cause me to dwell in peace and happiness.
Next, one should offer pure scented water.
Write [the mantra] on a leaf with a small amount of water and offer it.
The mantra is: Oṃ amṛte hūṃ phaṭ. The mantra for the scented unguent is:
Plucking with the middle finger, offer a small amount of scented ointment while reciting:
*Namo samantabuddhānāṃ viśuddhagaganasvabhāvāya svāhā*. The mantra for the flower garland (*mālā*) is as follows:
Conversely, with the hands joined in the *añjali* mudrā and placed at the forehead, rotate them to the right.
The mantra for incense is: *Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ mahāmaitry-abhyudgate svāhā*. The mantra for burning incense is as follows:
The earth, water, and fire elements face away from one another;
the two wind elements join at their sides;
and the space element pinches the upper joint of the wind-wheels, leaving it open.
Namo samantabuddhānāṃ amṛtodbhavāya svāhā. The mantra for food and drink is: *Mihap*.
Namo samanta-buddhānām. Ara ara kara kara mara mara dara dara vara vara dhara dhara hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. This is the mantra of the lamp-light offering.
Form a fist with the right hand, extending the fire-finger (middle finger) upright.

Press the space-finger (ring finger) against the wind-finger (little finger), and pinch the middle joint of the fire-finger. *Namo samantabuddhānāṃ tathāgataraśmispharaṇavyavasānagaganārciṣe svāhā*. This is the mantra for the Universal Offering of the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha.

Namo sarvatathāgatebhyo viśvamukhebhyaḥ svāhā | Khaṃ ṅaṃ naṃ te saparṇiṃ akāśagocare svāhā | Visualize that the World-Protecting Heavenly Kings each descend from their celestial palaces and arrive here.
Relying on the original directions, fix the mind upon them and address them by name with reverence:
"O Guardian Kings of the Directions and the deities of the twelve palaces."
The Nine Planets, the Great Devas, the Twenty-eight Lunar Mansions,
the lords of the karmic paths, the dark palaces, and the tutelary stars of my birth—
now that I have encountered these calamities and transformations, [I take refuge].
I respectfully thank the assembly of devas for their forbearance regarding my transgressions;
I entreat you to follow the Buddha’s instructions and accept my invitation.
May you all come to this assembly and respond to this call;
with single-minded sincerity, arouse a heart of joy,
and for the sake of me, [name], pacify all calamities and obstacles.
To increase merit and longevity, it is said:
"From this day forward, for a period of [number] days,
I shall recite the mantra of [deity]."
During this time, may the sanctuary be protected and all obstacles and difficulties be eliminated.
Regarding other matters, I, [Name], declare that I rely upon the power of the Great Sage’s protective mindfulness.
May you deliver us and all sentient beings from the karmic suffering of saṃsāra.
We pray that you, the Lord of the Direction who traverses the sky with the lunar mansions and planets,
will uphold the turning of the Buddha’s teachings and grant us fearlessness so that we may dwell in peace and happiness.
Having thus made the request,
one should next offer pure water from a ritual flask upon the leaves as an offering.
The mantra is as follows:

*Namo samantabuddhānām* (Namo sanman da muduo nan). *Indra-śa-ākṣam*. Next, snap the middle and ring fingers to offer a small amount of scented water (*gandha*). As soon as it is offered, say: "I offer [this]."
Next, place a single flower upon the seat.
The offering of flowers is called *puṣpa* (in transcription: *p'u-shih-erh-ho k'an-p'u-k'an-fan*).
Incense to be burned before the seat is, in Sanskrit, *dhūpa*.
Recite the "Du-yin-bu-gan" (度引補甘) incantation twice.
Next, place one ladle of gruel upon the leaf.
Again, say: "It has not yet arrived."
Next, take a small wax candle and insert it into the porridge. In Sanskrit: *Nirvāṇaputraśrīnivāpudraśāntikuru svāhā*.
After each person has completed the offerings from water to the candle, they should face [the deity].
Next, one should mentally offer the candles to all the honored ones;
do not allow the candles to go out until the offerings have been completed for everyone.
Alternatively, one may require assistants to dispatch several people,
each to attend to a specific task; if one were to perform these tasks oneself one by one, [it would be difficult].
I fear that if the candle does not last until the conclusion of the Dharma service, it may be inauspicious;
I request permission to perform the rite once more,
or perhaps to circumambulate [the altar].
Alternatively, one may sit upright and recite the mantra of Mahāśrī twenty-one times,
and further recite the mantra of Buddha-maitrī-rakṣa one hundred and eight times.
By means of this recitation, may all the devas be benefited;
may the joy of the devas increase ever more and more.
During the interval of making offerings, much was not in accordance with the Dharma.
"I only pray that you will, out of compassion, grant me joy.
The Master should hold the incense burner, universally seek joy, and entreat for the absence of calamity.
[He] recites the verse to dispatch the Lord of Heaven and the various devas through their sovereign majestic power.
Now, may those who seek [your aid] quickly achieve success.
We only pray that after you, O Lord of Devas, have returned to your original palace,
you will deign to come when invoked with compassion.
Oṃ giri-giri vajra muḥ svāhā. Next, offer food to all the spirits and deities (*bhūta*).
As stated in the *Subāhu-paripṛcchā-sūtra*:
Furthermore, Subāhu,
if a practitioner of recitation desires to achieve accomplishment in performing and upholding various dharmas, so that they may obtain siddhi without obstacles or difficulties,
they should offer various foods and drinks as sacrifices to the devas, asuras, yakṣas, nāga kings, kinnaras, garuḍas, kaṭapūtanas, gandharvas, bhūtas, and all other malevolent spirits.
Whether dwelling upon the earth or abiding in the void,
they shall cause the practitioner of recitation to be free from all obstacles and ensure that whatever they seek according to their wishes is entirely fulfilled.
Securely bind the mantra-seals (mudrā) for protection.
Kneeling with the right knee on the ground, one should address the petition, saying:
"O gods and bhūtas dwelling upon Mount Sumeru..."
They dwell in the Nandana Grove and other celestial palaces;
or they dwell in the sun and moon,
or in rivers, seas, marshes, ponds, springs, and wells.
Some dwell in villages;
some dwell in shrines;
some dwell in empty rooms.
Some dwell in celestial palaces;
some reside in monasteries or caityas;
and some live in thatched huts of non-Buddhist practitioners.
Some dwell in houses;
some dwell in storehouses;
some reside in streets and alleys.
Some dwell by the side of a crossroads;
some rely on a solitary tree;
some stay by a great road.
Some dwell among burial mounds;
some reside in the Śmaśāna forest;
and some take up residence in the great forest.
Some dwell in places where lions and tigers roam;
some reside in great sandy deserts;
and some inhabit the most excellent and sublime locations on islands in the ocean.
May you, together with all your attendants and retinues, deign to descend and come here.
I have prepared flower garlands, unguents, food and drink, and exquisite lamps;
may you graciously grant your presence.
The matters for which I have sought and prayed shall be fulfilled.
As for the fruit [of this], one should place various kinds of sweet food, drink, cakes, and crisp sweets within a copper vessel or a clean jar.
All must be broken into small pieces.
Recite the mantra for bestowing food upon the hungry ghosts (Yamāntaka-preta-bhojana-mantra) while giving rise to a mind of compassion.
Place your hand upon the basin and perform the empowerment twenty-one times.
Furthermore, recite the mantra of the Tathāgata of Sublime Form.
Sprinkle consecrated water and recite the mantra of the Universal Offering Mudrā. With sincere devotion,
invoke and seek out abundant, exquisite, and refined offerings of flowers, incense, and food for the worship.
Furthermore, he recited this verse:
"By the merit I have cultivated, may it universally reach those in the realm of hungry ghosts;
having eaten, may they be freed from the suffering of hunger, and upon casting off their bodies, be reborn in a place of bliss."
One should then scatter [the food] outside the enclosure or in various directions within the house,
or cast it into a long-flowing stream,
giving it as food for nameless spirits and deities to consume.

I take refuge in all the Buddhas and Śakra.
I accept this offering of *argha*, unguents, flower garlands, incense, rice porridge, and exquisite lamps.
May the Auspicious Devaputra bring about the pacification of calamities for [Name].
May merit and wisdom increase and flourish;
may all be auspicious and perfect. Therefore, it is said: *svāhā*.
Regarding the mantras, mudrās, and other rites for bestowing offerings upon the celestial kings of the ten directions:
whenever one receives various teachings, completes a session of recitation, performs *homa*, or undergoes consecration (*abhiṣeka*),
it is essential in all such cases to offer these gifts to the deities so that one may swiftly attain freedom from obstacles.
The verse says:
Contemplating that the mind arises as the dharma-dhātu,
one accomplishes the three-cornered *nāga*-shaped mandala of the original wrathful deity, fiercely blazing and piercing through to the Brahma-heaven.
The sequence for the three families... [blank]... recite the mantra for summoning with the cord four times and for the accomplishment of the body three times. Alternatively, [one may recite] once...
when the ritual is finished and the vow has been made, subsequently seal the deities of the original direction.

Each recites their own root mantra; having completed the ritual recitation according to the dharma by escorting the holy ones to protect the directions, and having finished the songs of praise and the making of vows,
one releases the boundary, escorts the holy devas, and then exits the site of practice.
On an eight-cornered circular altar, establish the positions for the ten holy ones;
place the Brahmā and Earth deities to the left and right of Śakra,
or alternatively, in the direction of the Nāgas, placing them opposite the Brahmā and Earth deities.
The positions of the Sun and Moon deities, and all the planets and lunar mansions, revolve around the central position.
Visualize the four arms of the immovable wrathful king:
his two hands form vajra-fists, with the wind and earth fingers curved like hooks.
With the two sides of the mouth secured, the right hand hooks while the left holds the cord;
Mount Sumeru serves as the seat. Outside the body appear eight peaks, with sharp and keen vajra-wheels, vast and full, of deep blue-black color.
With disheveled hair hanging loose, his majestic flames are like the conflagration at the end of an eon;
his power is like that of a garuḍa, so brilliant and resplendent that none can face him.
Māras and pātālas, seized by terror, flee in all directions.
Relying on the power of former great vows, you manifest these forms of violent ferocity to swallow up all obstacles and afflictions, and to comfort those who practice the path.
Having arrayed yourselves in their respective positions, we offer this mixed gruel as an oblation.
Boil non-glutinous rice, sesame seeds, and mung beans together;
then, at each of the various altar sites,
place a porcelain vessel and pour a small amount of pure scented water into it.
Next, offer [the food] with [a respectful mind]; use the fingers to snap them together;
again, offer various famous flowers; next, burn incense;
and then, with a single ladle of porridge, all performed with a heart of profound sincerity.
Perform the empowerment three times for each. Next, hold a small wax candle over the congee;
do not let this candle go out until the rite is completed.
[Focus] upon the character "Perfectly Quiescent" (yuanji).
Add the words of the prayer you seek: "Through the secret empowerment of the Noble One's power, may all that is done be accomplished. This shall assist my practice;
even my solitary aspirations shall be attained. When you wish to request [the deity] to bestow [grace], [recite this].
Fixing the mind to establish its station, One should perform offerings according to the ritual;
With resolute freedom from doubt, All aspirations shall be fulfilled.
The nine planets have the Sun as their lord, And all the lunar mansions have the Moon as their lord.
Brahmabhūmi-mudrā: Now I shall explain in sequence the eight-petaled *padma*.
The *mṛḍa-homa* mudrā is like the *argha* [offering], with ten fingers; it is the earth-goddess *mṛḍa*.
Firmly grasping the wrist of wisdom with the hand of concentration, the fingers of wisdom are extended upright;
the thumb (the wheel of space) enters the moon (the palm) horizontally, while the ring finger (the wind element) moves back and forth like a hook.
This is the seal for requesting the Fire Deity to send [the guest]. Then, holding the meditation finger (the little finger) with the precept finger (the index finger).
Facing outward, snap the fingers three times; this is the mantra for dispatching the *mātṛkā* as explained in the sūtra.

[The Sanskrit names for the ten titles of the Tathāgata’s virtues: *Tathāgata*, *Arhat*, *Samyaksaṃbuddha*, *Vidyācaraṇasaṃpanna*, *Sugata*, *Lokavid*, *Anuttarapuruṣadamyasārathi*, *Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām*, *Buddha*, and *Bhagavān*. First, perform the sequence of offerings to the World-Honored One outside the maṇḍala.
Spread out mats of *kuśa* grass, lotus leaves, or green grass, and smear the circular mandala;
prepare the six types of requisites, such as wax candles and so forth.
Next, take your seat and don the armor of the three families to protect the body.

Next, empower the scented water by reciting the mantra of the Kīlikīla mudrā twenty-one times and sprinkle it over the offerings and other items in the four directions. Then, empower them seven times using the karma mudrā.
Next, for the consecration of the maṇḍala, recite the Kīlikīla mantra seven or twenty-one times.
Then, purify the ground according to the great ritual procedure. Next, recite the five great vows and set forth the purpose of the undertaking.
Furthermore, when reciting the Prajñāpāramitā sūtras, [one invokes] the various devas and others.
Next, regarding the site for the mandala of the Great Wheel Vajra Seal and Mantra, one visualizes that within the mandala, the syllable *Ṭa* transforms into a single-pronged vajra.

The pestle transforms into the Four-Armed Vidyārāja as described in the *Homa* ritual; next, one should visualize the four-syllable mantra according to the *Mahāvidhi*, such that the primordial resident deity bestows empowerment upon the central deity within the maṇḍala, merging them into non-dual union.
Next, invoke [the deities] according to their respective directions and recite the mantra of the Great Hook-summoning Seal (*mahā-ākarṣaṇa-mudrā*).
The mantra is as follows:

*Namaḥ samantabuddhānām, āḥ kṣi huḥ sarvatrā pratihataiḥ, tathāgataguhyaiḥ, candrajvālāparipūrakaiḥ, svāhā*. Next, recite the Sanskrit names to request [their presence]. Then, kneeling on the right knee, recite the words of invitation and perform the complete ritual procedures according to the rules.
If it is too extensive, it is better not to recite it. Next, recite the praise of the four wisdoms (*catur-jñāna*).
Next, hold up the *argha* vessel and offer it to Acala Vidyārāja. Next, perform the seat mudrā (*āsana-mudrā*). Next, the net mudrā (*jāla-mudrā*).

Next, [perform] the fire offering (*homa*). Next, apply ointments and burn flowers. Recite as usual and offer them to Acala. Next, make offerings one by one to the various deities; according to their respective directions, place a vessel for each. Next is the mantra for universal offering.
Next, perform the mudrā-binding to empower the five places.
Next, recite the mantra of Acala Maitreya one hundred and eight times.
Having recited the earnest prayers and counted them,
perform the protective binding and repentance as before;
next, recite the mantra of the presiding deity one hundred and eight times.
If one recites it one thousand and eighty times,
it may be used as a protective empowerment for the patron.
Next, one should recite the Tathāgata-maitrī-rakṣā-mantra one hundred and eight times.
Furthermore, it is the meaning of dedicating the merit by reciting the Great Auspicious Celestial Mantra one hundred and eight times.
Following that, one makes offerings and presents them to Acala Vidyārāja.
Next, one recites the Universal Offering Mantra to offer to the assembly of deities in the ocean-like gathering, the dust-motes of all buddha-fields, and the world-protecting devas.
Next are the praises of the four wisdoms and the praises of the eight classes of devas and nāgas.
Next is the dedication of merit.
Next is the dissolution of the boundary.
As in the preceding examples, each is explained individually.
Next, the *argha* offering;
next, the dismissal (*visarjana*).
Next is the protection of the body through the three families.
This is as previously described when first exiting the maṇḍala.
